column1: # The reviewed departures from the Arlington PDF Model, which tools/AdCodicem.Pdf.Arlington applies when it
# generates src/AdCodicem.Pdf/Validation/Arlington/ArlingtonModel.g.cs. Tab-separated; lines starting with # are
# comments. Object and Key may each list several names, separated by commas.
# Column says what an override does:
# - a column of the model (Type, SinceVersion, DeprecatedIn, Required, Inheritable, PossibleValues, Link): the cell
#   is replaced by Value, written in the model's own grammar, before the tables are built;
# - Findings, Value none: the row stays as the model has it, and the generated rules Rule lists stay silent on that
#   key, because a hand-written rule reports the fault: the Reason reads "covered by <that rule>";
# - Inheritance, Value AcroForm/DA: the walk also takes the key from the interactive form dictionary's /DA.
# Rule names the generated rules the override changes.
# The bar (ADR 44, as settled on 2026-09-28): a content override is made only when ISO 32000-1, the version the
# files declare, does not require what the model says, and its Reason quotes the text; a genuine ISO 32000-1
# violation stays a finding, declared in tests/corpus/manifest.json. A generator test fails when an override no
# longer changes the pinned model, or silences a rule the row can no longer give: it must then go.
# Checked against ISO 32000-1 and dropped: letting an Order sub-array (ArrayOfOptContentOrders) hold arrays, in
# its element 0 or after it. ISO 32000-1 8.11.4.3, Table 101 calls the nested arrays "Arrays of optional content
# groups which may be displayed by a conforming reader in a tree or outline structure" whose only other element is
# a first "text string to be used as a non-selectable label": a sub-array nested in a sub-array is not described,
# so Esri's stays a declared finding.
# Checked against ISO 32000-1 and dropped: letting a Type 3 font's Encoding be a name (FontType3/Encoding, Type and
# Link). ISO 32000-1 9.6.5, Table 112 gives its type as "name or dictionary", but the same row's text reads "(Required)
# An encoding dictionary whose Differences array shall specify the complete character encoding for this font": ISO
# 32000-1 requires the dictionary the model wants, so the AFP Batch Processor's /Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding stays a
# declared finding.
Object

column1: Resource
column6: ISO 32000-1 7.8.3 says "Each key in a resource dictionary shall be the name of a resource type, as shown in Table 33", and Table 33 has no Encoding: the row is PDF 1.0's named-encoding resource (its note reads "see Adobe PDF Reference 1.0, 6.8.3"), whose deprecation in 1.2 ISO 32000-1 does not state; Acrobat's AcroForm /DR reuses the name for its PDFDocEncoding dictionary
column7: 33 clean corpus documents and 8 others, every occurrence in an AcroForm /DR: Acrobat, PDFMaker, InDesign, LiveCycle, PageMaker, Word 365, LibreOffice 4.4, ReportLab 5.0.1, Quartz, PDFium, veraPDF test files
